humanities_role_explanation: Historical Czech books and periodicals (OCR'd archival pages) supply the texts, but the competence tested is generic NLP topic localization (span extraction given a topic name/description), not historical or disciplinary interpretation. Digital humanities is only a motivating application.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Text only. Scanned pages were converted by PERO-OCR into text segments of 768-1024 characters; models see only text.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Topic localization: identifying word-level spans expressing a human-defined topic (name plus description) in a text, evaluated at text level (topic presence detection, i.e. document-level classification) and word level (span localization, F1/IoU). Related to extractive QA and zero-shot span labeling, with tagging vs matching output paradigms.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Single-task benchmark scoped to topic localization in historical Czech documents.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: GPT-5-2, gpt-5-mini, gpt-5-nano, gpt-oss-20b, Llama 3.3 70B, Llama 3.2 3B, Gemma 3 27B/4B, Gemini 3 Pro preview; plus fine-tuned BERT-type encoders.

quantitative_metrics.note: Precision, recall, F1, IoU, localization success, Krippendorff's alpha, bootstrap CIs.

summary: The paper introduces CzechTopic, a human-annotated benchmark for zero-shot topic localization in OCR'd historical Czech documents, with human-defined topics and span annotations. Models are scored relative to average pairwise human agreement rather than a single gold; LLMs and BERT cross-encoders fine-tuned on an LLM-distilled development set are compared.
key_findings: Best LLM (gpt-5-2) reaches word-level F1 61.1 and IoU 48.7 vs human baseline 68.7 F1 and 57.2 IoU; at text level 80.6 vs 83.2 F1. Large variability across LLMs (best 61.1 vs worst 13.2 F1). Fine-tuned BERT models reach up to 48.3 word F1 (robeczech), beating smaller LLMs. Matching beats tagging by 0.104 F1; few-shot adds 0.010; prompt language has no effect. Krippendorff's alpha 0.616 (micro).
dataset_size: 525 texts (363 topics, 1,820 annotated text-topic pairs) in the human-annotated benchmark; a separate distilled development set has 15,550 texts
facets_explanation: Topics and spans were produced by multiple human annotators in two phases following written guidelines, but the paper does not state their disciplinary training, so the source is not_stated. Evaluation is explicitly relative to average pairwise human agreement rather than a single gold annotation, and the divergence between topic author and later annotators is analysed as informative about implicit topic interpretation. Answers are spans determined by the given text and topic description.
results_explanation: The best model gpt-5-2-2025-12-11 gets word-level F1 61.1 (IoU 48.7) against Human baseline 68.7 F1, giving a gap of 8 points (68.7-61.1=7.6, rounded). Text-level vs word-level F1 for gpt-5-2 is 80.6 vs 61.1 (about 19 points); for llama3-3-70b 75.2 vs 53.0 gives 22 points, used as the largest depth-type gap. Ablations (few-shot vs zero-shot 0.010 F1) record input-type comparisons.
